title: Line Tack on Garment
content: ### Objective Create lines on Garment and tack to each other by lines / shapes. (Ver. MD7) ### Location 3D window tool bar Line tack tool ### Operation 1. Select the tool according to the Location above. 2. Mouse over to a garment from 3D window. Point follows mouse cursor. 3. Double click on the garment where want to create start point of line / shape. Double click to complete the line / shape Double click on start point of line to create closed shape. 4. Create second line/ shape. Once all the two lines / shapes have been created, connection line for line / shape will be displayed. 5. Click the simulation button. Two lines/ shapes tack to each other along the connection line. * During the creation of the line, pressing the Shift key will display the front, back, side center line and guide line of last point. * Press the Ctrl key to create curved line. * When creating a line, can cancel it from the last point by pressing the Delete key on Keyboard. Press the Esc / Ctrl+Z to cancel the whole point.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Line Tack Tool in the 3D window to create and connect lines and shapes on garments effectively.

title: TOPSTITCH PROPERTIES: Extend Topstitch
content: ### Objective When the start or end point of a Topstitch does not reach or sticks out of the Pattern outline, extend it to fit to the Pattern. When using the Free Topstitch tool, the starting point is going to be the first click point. ### Location Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Extend Start / Extend End ### Operation 1. Select a Topstitch with Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Extend Start / Extend End
content_description: This web page provides instructions for adjusting the start and end points of a Topstitch to align with the Pattern outline using the Topstitch Property Editor.

title: Custom View
content: ### Objective Easily open and save custom view of the 3D window at your convenience. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View ### Operation #### Create 1. Rotate the 3D Window as desired. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View →The Custom View window appears. 3. Left click on the camera icon on the right top corner. → The current view is saved and added to the Custom View window. 4. Double click on the added custom view. → The 3D Window rotates automatically to reflect the custom view. #### Open/Save 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View → The Custom View window appears. 2. Add the desired custom view. 3. Click on the Open or the Save All button. → The group of custom views is opened or saved. #### Delete 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View → The Custom View window appears. 2. Add the desired custom view. 3. Right-click on the custom view to be deleted. →The right-click pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Delete. → The selected custom view is deleted from the Custom View window. #### Rename 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View → The Custom View window appears. 2. Add the desired custom view. 3. Right click on the custom view to be deleted. →The right click pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Rename. → Edit the name as the custom view's name field is activated. ※ Note: Starting from ver4.1.0, Delete All or Overwrite custom views using the right-click pop-up menu.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to easily create, open, save, delete, and rename custom views of a 3D window for enhanced visualization and convenience.

title: Flatten
content: ### Objective Extract Patterns based on lines and shapes created on an Avatar. ※ Note: The Flattening function only extracts closed shapes as Patterns. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Flatten 3D Toolbar ▶ Flatten ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Flatten 3D Toolbar ▶ Flatten → Points no longer appear and only lines appear on the Avatar. 2. Hover the mouse over the shape to be extracted as a Pattern. → The area to be flattened appears in light blue. 3. Select all areas to be extracted by holding Shift on the keyboard, then clicking on the desired areas. → The selected areas are highlighted in yellow. 4. Press the Enter key to execute **Flatten (Separate)**. → The selected areas on the Avatar are converted to patterns and appear in both the 3D and 2D windows. → The default Fabric is applied to all Patterns created with the Flatten tool. → Sewing lines are automatically established for adjacent Patterns. → The lines remain on the Avatar. 5. Press the Shift + Enter key to execute **Flatten (Merge)**. → If adjacent surfaces are selected, a single merged pattern will be created.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for extracting patterns from an Avatar using the Flatten tool in the 3D Garment feature.

title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Show/Hide Individual Tape Measure
content: ### Objective Show or hide tape measure individually. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Bottom of the Avatar Editor Window ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Bottom of the Avatar Editor Window 2. Click the check-box to turn it On or Off.
content_description: This web page provides users with the ability to individually show or hide the tape measure in the Avatar Editor for enhanced customization.

title: Edit Curvature
content: ### ### ### ### ### ### Objective Convert a straight line to a curved line or edit a curved line's curvature. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curvature 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Curvature ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curvature 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Curvature 2. Click and drag a straight line to convert it to a curved line. → AI Bezier handles are added to the both end of the selected line. 3. Or, click and drag a curved line to edit the curvature.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for converting straight lines to curved lines and editing the curvature of existing curved lines in a 2D design tool.

title: System Requirements (July 2025)
content: # **Applicable for: All users of Marvelous Designer software** In this document, Marvelous Designer or Marvelous Designer software refers only to the Marvelous Designer software installed on the user's local computer, and does not refer to CLO-SET and various other CLO products. The hardware components presented in the documents and tables below have been tested directly by Marvelous Designer team or are listed based on feedback from Marvelous Designer users. Please note that Marvelous Designer team does not provide consulting services such as computer price quotes and hardware performance comparisons. So please carefully review the Marvelous Designer software installation and operating conditions described below. # **Windows** Category | **Minimum** | **Recommended** ---|---|--- OS | Windows 10 64-bit (1903 or later) | Windows 10 64-bit (22H2) 1) 2) 3) Windows 11 64-bit (24H2) Processor | AMD® Ryzen™ 5 1500X Intel® Core-i5 6400 | AMD® Ryzen™ 7/9 7000 series or higher Intel® Core-i7/i9 14th Gen or higher Memory | 8GB | 32GB or more 5 4) Graphics card | NVIDIA® GeForce GTX 960 orNVIDIA® Quadro P2200 | NVIDIA® GeForce RTX series or NVIDIA® Quadro RTX , RTX A, RTX Ada series 5) 6) 7) Storage | HDD 10GB or more | SSD 20GB or more Screen | 1920x1080(FHD) | 2560x1440(QHD), 3840x2160(UHD, 4K) Input device | 3-button mouse | 3-button mouse Network | Internet connection required | Internet connection required 1) Windows updates and patches are highly recommended. [Windows Update - Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/install-windows-updates-3c5ae7fc-9fb6-9af1-1984-b5e0412c556a) 2) If dll-related errors occur while installing or running Marvelous Designer, install the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable. X64 architecture is recommended. [Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable latest supported downloads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-170) 3) Marvelous Designer software cannot run on Windows 10/11 N which media features removed. Download and install the Media Feature Pack from the Microsoft website. [Media Feature Pack for Windows 10/11 N (February 2023)](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/media-feature-pack-for-windows-10-11-n-february-2023-2aaf89b8-f9d3-4322-98d0-612c9bea9c01) 4) For smoother operation, 16GB or more of memory is recommended. 32GB or more of memory is recommended if you are using multiple software at the same time and/or dealing with huge and complex garments. 5) Marvelous Designer utilizes [Nvidia CUDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA) acceleration technology for Marvelous Designer GPU-Simulation and Rendering. So computers with only Intel Graphics or AMD graphics card do not benefit from GPU acceleration that speeds up Marvelous Designer simulation. If you want faster GPU-simulation in Marvelous Designer software, look for a computer with a recent Nvidia graphics card. 6) For graphics card related issues, please see the following guide. In particular, please update your graphics card driver to the latest. [Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358166752793) 7) A GPU that supports OpenGL Compatibility Profile 1.3 or higher is required to run Marvelous Designer software. Some mobile GPU processors from AMD and Intel may not fully support [OpenGL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenGL), which is essential for running Marvelous Designer software, and may not run Marvelous Designer software. If you are using a laptop or graphics card with a built-in CPU, check with the hardware manufacturer for the GPU model and whether it supports OpenGL. * * * # # **Mac** Category | **Minimum** | **Recommended** ---|---|--- Mac models | All Macs released after 2016 1) 2) | Apple Silicon Macs: M1, M2, M3, M4 macOS | Monterey 12 *For macOS dependencies, check out the notes below 3) | Ventura 13, Sonoma 14, Sequoia 15 Processor | Intel® Core-i5 4cores | Apple Silicon 4) 5) Memory | 8GB | 24GB or more Storage | HDD 10GB or more | SSD 20GB or more Screen | 1280x800 | Retina 4K, Retina 5K supported Input devices | 3-button mouse | 3-button mouse Network | Internet connection required | Internet connection required 1) Starting with Marvelous Designer 2024, the minimum macOS has been changed to Monterey 12. See which macs are compatible with macOS Monterey 12 here. [macOS Monterey is compatible with these computers.](https://support.apple.com/en-us/103260) 2) Intel chip macs do not have Nvidia graphics cards, so mac users cannot make use of GPU acceleration, but simulation and rendering are supported normally. 3) macOS dependencies * Sierra 10.12: users can install and run up to Marvelous Designer 9. * High Sierra 10.13: users can install and run up to Marvelous Designer 10. * Mojave 10.14: users can install and run up to Marvelous Designer 10. * Catalina 10.15: users can install and run up to Marvelous Designer 12. * Please note that Marvelous Designer 11 and future versions will not run on macOS Mojave or earlier. 4) As of Marvelous Designer 11, provides as a compatible build for both Apple Silicon macs and Intel chip macs. If you want to use version 10 or lower on Apple Silicon Mac, you need to install Apple Rosetta. Visit here for more info. [If you need to install Rosetta on your Mac: Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/102527) * * * ## # **See also** * Marvelous Designer software does not support garment pattern digitizers. * Marvelous Designer software have tested and supports Wacom® tablet products, and compatibility issues may occur with third-party tablets. * Marvelous Designer software does not support BootCamp in macOS, also does not support similar desktop virtualization apps. * Marvelous Designer software does not support 32-bit OS (e.g. Windows 7 32-bit), Apple iOS, iPad OS, tvOS, Android OS, ChromeOS, Windows Mobile and Linux. * Marvelous Designer software can be downloaded as .exe or .dmg file format via [Marvelous Designer official website](https://marvelousdesigner.com/product/download). It is not distributed in .msi or .pkg file format. * Marvelous Designer software can be installed and run in virtual server environments such as Virtual Machine and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure and in cloud services. However, in this case, Marvelous Designer team does not provide technical support.
content_description: This webpage provides essential hardware and software requirements for users of Marvelous Designer to ensure optimal performance and compatibility.

title: MODULAR MODE: General Process of Using Modular Mode
content: Follow the procedure of the Modular Mode to build and design with your own Pattern database. To build the Pattern database, take following procedures: Open Modular Template ▶ Add Patterns or Garments ▶ Drag the Patterns into Block Boxes ▶ Sew the Patterns and the Block Boxes ▶ Save it as a Block file (If there is no Modular file in a folder where the Blocks are being saved, save a Modular file too)
content_description: "Learn how to create and customize your own Pattern database using the Modular Mode with a step-by-step guide."

title: Create 2D Graphic Measurement
content: ### Objective View graphic position from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements. (ver2.5.0) ### Location Graphics ▶ Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurement ### Operation 1. 2D Toolbar ▶Select a graphic with Transform Graphic. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Graphics ▶ Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurement 3. Select the desired 2D measurement option. To Center | View the 2D measurements from the center of the graphic to left/right/top/bottom of the Pattern outline. ---|--- To Outline | View the 2D measurements from the left/right/top/bottom of the graphic to the Pattern outline. → The 2D measurements are now being displayed accordingly.
content_description: This web page provides users with step-by-step instructions to view and manipulate 2D measurements of graphics in relation to a Pattern outline using the Property Editor.

title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Rename Topstitch
content: ### Objective Rename Topstitches. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Rename ### Operation 1. Object Browser ▶ Select a Topstitch style to rename. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Rename → The name is now being changed and applied.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for renaming Topstitch styles using the Property Editor in the Object Browser.

title: Lock Remesh Patterns
content: ### Objective Lock patterns from selection based on whether or not they are dynamic Marvelous Designer patterns with adjustable particle distance and curve points, or remeshed patterns created with the Topology Tools & Remesh All. * * * ### Location 2D Pattern Window ▶ Lock Pattern Drop-down Menu ▶ Lock All Remesh Patterns ### Operation 1. Load a garment. 2. Create topology with the 'Create Topology' Tool in the 2D Pattern Window. 3. When complete, with blue retopology still visible, Right Mouse Button Click in the 2D Pattern Window then select 'Remesh All (duplicate)'. → Retopology meshes are placed directly on top of the original patterns. 4. Click on 'Lock All Remesh Patterns' in the Lock Pattern drop-down menu within the 2D Window to lock all remeshed patterns from selection. → Click and move original patterns as desired with the 'Transform Pattern' Tool. → Click on 'Unlock All Remesh Patterns' to release the selection mask. 5. Click on 'Lock All Pattern Outlines' and 'Lock All Internal Lines' to lock original patterns from selection. → Click and move remeshed patterns as desired with the 'Transform Pattern' Tool.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for locking and managing dynamic and remeshed patterns in Marvelous Designer, enhancing workflow efficiency in garment design.

title: Curved Side Geometry
content: ### Objective Apply and adjust curvature on edges of Patterns for more natural and realistic look (ver2.2.0). ### Location 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern ### Operation 1. Firstly, change the 3D Garment rendering style to Thick Textured Surface in the 3D window. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 3. Select a Pattern or Pattern line to express curved sided effect. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 4. Enter a desired value at: Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶ Curved Side Geometry ▶ Curvature (%) → The curvature is now being applied according to the entered value. ※ Note: The maximum Curvature (%) value is 50 percent (%) of the fabric thickness. For instance, if the fabric thickness is being set at 1mm, the maximum Curvature (%) is 0.5mm.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for applying and adjusting curvature on pattern edges to achieve a more natural and realistic appearance in garment design.

title: Free Topstitch
content: ### Objective Create a Topstitch to freely sew regardless of the points of Pattern or Internal Shape. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Free Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Free Topstitch ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Free Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Free Topstitch 2. Click on a point where a Topstitch begins. 3. Move mouse to the direction where the Topstitch is going to be created. → The selected area appears in red color. 4. Click on another point where the Topstitch ends. → The tTopstitch is now created with being highlighted. ※ Note: * Click-and-drag in the 2D window to encompass all segments where Topstitches to be applied. Topstitches appear on all selected segments (ver3.2.0). * Use lasso selection to select Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Topstitches should be created on (ver3.2.0). * OBJ Topstitches temporarily disappear when the Simulation is activated, but they appear again when the Simulation is deactivated (ver3.2.0). * Right click when creating the Topstitch to enter specific length (ver4.2.0).
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to create and apply Topstitches freely within their designs, enhancing their sewing experience with intuitive tools and features.

title: Trace as / Convert to Internal Shape
content: ### Objective Use the Trace function to convert selected lines/shapes or areas into Internal Lines/Shapes. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Line (3D Pattern) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Line (3D Pattern) 2. Click on created Baselines or Internal Lines on 3D Garment. → The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now highlighted in yellow. 3. Right-click on the selected Baselines or Internal Lines. → A Pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Trace as Internal Shape or Convert to Internal Shape in the pop-up menu. → The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now being traced as /converted to Internal Shapes.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on using the Trace function to convert selected lines and shapes into Internal Lines and Shapes within the 3D Toolbar.

title: Refresh Texture
content: ### Objective Edit texture images with an image editing tool and save over the original image with the same name and file location, press Refresh button to instantly apply the changes of the Fabric's texture images. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D/2D Window Background Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶ Refresh Textures
content_description: "Effortlessly edit and update texture images in real-time using our intuitive image editing tool, ensuring seamless changes with a simple refresh."

title: Create Multiple Patterns or Internal Shapes and Input Intervals
content: ### Objective Designate the number of shapes and input the interval when creating Patterns or Internal Lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Applicable Tools 2D Toolbar ▶ Applicable Tools ※ Note: * Applicable tools are as follows: Rectangle tool, Internal Rectangle tool, Ellipse tool, Internal Ellipse tool. ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline as below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Applicable Tool 2D Toolbar ▶ Applicable Tools 2. Click once on the 2D window. → The pop-up window with options to create the selected Pattern or Internal Shape appears. 3. Enter desired values for options below the Replicate category and click OK. Name | Description ---|--- Number of Shapes | Set the number of replicated shapes. Interval | Set the distance between each Pattern or Internal Shape/Line. Angle | Set the direction that the replicated Patterns are placed. → The Patterns or Internal Shapes/Lines are replicated based on the settings.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and customizing Patterns or Internal Lines in 2D design by specifying the number of shapes, intervals, and angles.

title: Activate/Deactivate Sewing Lines
content: ### Objective Activate or deactivate Sewing Lines as needed. Use this function when Sewing Lines should be applied after the garment is draped, such as the back slits for a men's jacket. ### Location 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected) → Deactivated Sewing Lines appear in white in the 2D and the 3D window.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for activating or deactivating Sewing Lines in garment design, allowing for adjustments post-draping, such as for back slits in men's jackets.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Bending-Weft/Warp
content: ### Objective Use Bending intensity which is the resistant against being bent, to adjust the stiffness of fabric. The higher the value, the stiffer it becomes such as denim and leather, and the lower the value, the more it becomes suitable for draping materials such as silk. The Bending intensity for the weft and warp directions can be set separately like the real fabrics. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Preset ▶ Bending-Weft/Warp Expressing materials with Weft (Horizontal) bending intensity ![B](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438785219737) Expressing materials with Warp (Vertical) bending intensity ![B](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438801346585)
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on adjusting the bending intensity of fabrics to control stiffness and draping characteristics in the Fabric Property Editor of your design software.

title: Polygon Lasso Selection
content: ### Objective Select Patterns, Sewing Lines, Topstitches, and Puckering with more freedom. Location Main Menu ▶ Edit tool for the respective item 3D/ 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit tool for the respective item ※ Note: Edit Tools for Respective Items --- Pattern | Transform Pattern (A) Line/Point | Edit Pattern (Z) Sewing | Edit Sewing (B) Topstitches | Edit Topstitch (J) Buttons/Buttonholes | Select/Move Button ([) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Edit tool for the respective item 3D/ 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit tool for the respective item 2. Double click in the 2D window, then drag the mouse. → A selection point appears where the mouse is double clicked and a line follows as the mouse is dragged. → The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers; by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) 3. Click around the items to create the lasso selection. 4. Click on the start point to complete the lasso selection. → All items related to the Edit tool are selected and highlighted in yellow. ※ Note: Only items related to the activated Edit tool are selected. For example, if the Edit Pattern tool is used to create a polygon lasso selection, only segments and points within the lasso selection are selected.
content_description: "Enhance your design workflow by easily selecting and editing patterns, sewing lines, topstitches, and buttons with our intuitive editing tools."

title: 1:N Segment Sewing (2D)
content: ### Objective Easily sew multiple segments (N) to a single segment (1.) If the total length of N segments and the length of 1 segment are different, the 1 segment is equally divided by the number of N segments. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Segment Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Segment Sewing 2. Select a single segment which multiple segments are sewn to. 3. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to hover over the N segments. Before clicking the segment, be careful to make Directional Notches parallel to each other. 5. Then, click on the segments to establish Sewing Lines on the N segments. 6. Release the Shift key to complete the 1:N Segment Sewing. ※ Note * The difference in lengths between the first and second half seams appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. When the difference is greater than 1 inch, it turns red to alert the user. * While establishing 1:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the sewing line cannot be applied. * While establishing N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for efficiently sewing multiple segments to a single segment while ensuring proper alignment and length adjustments.

title: Create Buttons along Pattern Outline
content: ### Objective Create buttons along a Pattern Outline in a constant interval and distance. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Button 3D toolbar ▶ Button ### Operation #### Create 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Right-click on the outline of the pattern. → The button/buttonhole creation option window appears along the pattern outline. ※Note: Hold down the Shift key and left-click on a segment to select multiple. 3. Set each option and click OK. Type | Start Position | Repeatedly create a button based on the starting point. ---|---|--- Distribute | Create by aligning buttons at regular intervals between the starting and ending points. Based on Start | Start Position | Distance | Adjust the distance between the clicked segment and the center of the button. Interval | Adjust the spacing between the pattern outline and the center of the button. Reverse | The starting point of the button and replicated created direction are adjusted in reverse. Replicate | Interval | Adjust the distance between the buttons. Number of Buttons/Buttonholes | Adjust the number of buttons. Distribute (ver. 11) | Position | Distance | Adjust the distance between the clicked segment and t he center of the button. Start/End Interval | Adjust the spacing between the pattern outline and the center of the start/end buttons. Replicate | Number of Buttons/Buttonholes | Enter the number of buttons/buttonholes to align between the start and end points. #### → A group button is created. #### Select 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click a button or segment created along the pattern outline. → All grouped buttons are selected. 3. Change the button properties and style or right-click. → Applied to grouped buttons. → Group information is not copied/pasted. ※Note: * If clicking again on the selected group button, it is able to select a button individually. * Grouped buttons cannot be moved. #### Unlink 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. After right-clicking on a button or segment created along the pattern outline and click Unlink Buttons/Buttonholes. → The group is unlinked.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for creating, selecting, and managing buttons along a pattern outline in a design tool.

title: 3D Seamline
content: ### Objective Adjust Intensity and Thickness of 3D seamlines to render a realistic Garment. ### Location Select Sewing Line ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Seamline ### Operation 1. Select the Edit Sewing tool from the 2D/3D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Sewing Line ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Seamline 3. Adjust the settings below as needed: Option | Description ---|--- Normal Map | Intensity (%) | Adjust the intensity of the Normal Map applied to the seamline. Thickness | Adjust the thickness of the Normal Map applied to the seamline.
content_description: This web page guides users on how to adjust the intensity and thickness of 3D seamlines for realistic garment rendering.

title: MODULAR MODE: Sew Blocks
content: ### Objective Set seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes. ### Location Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor ### Operation Sew Patterns and Block Boxes 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 2\. Click on Segment sewing tool or Free sewing tool. 3\. Set seamlines for Pattern and its relative Block Boxes (Step 2 and 3 do not necessarily need to be in order). 4.Set Pattern outlines (Patterns must be sewn one another i.e. shoulder seams, armholes, side seams) and seamlines between Block Boxes. 5\. Repeat the steps above for the remains. ※ Note: * Block Boxes can only be sewn with Segment Sewing. In other words, sewing multiple Block Box segments at once by using M:N Free Sewing is not allowed. Therefore if the number of Block Box segments is higher than the number of segments need to be sewn, add segments on the patterns to make the number equal, then sew them 1:1. ex) In case of a basic t-shirt block, there is a point added on the neck segment. Therefore add a point on its pattern, then sew the segments 1:1. * Patterns that are sewn alone (i.e. hems, sleeves or armholes of a sleeveless style) do not need to be sewn to Block Boxes. * Difference in length between the actual Pattern and the Block Boxes has no effect on the simulation. * Rest of the principle is the same as the Simulation Mode. Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 2\. 2D Toolbar default presets Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing tool. → While the tool is toggled on, it enables to check the seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes. 3\. Deselect Show modular sewing / Show pattern sewing tool. → Block Boxes to Pattern seamlines disappears but for Patterns to Patterns are appeared. ※ Note: If seamlines do not appear after setting Pattern and Block Boxes, please confirm Show modular sewing / Show pattern sewing toggle status.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for setting seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes in the Modular Mode Block Editor.

title: Delete Bounding Voulme
content: ### Objective Delete Bounding Volume no longer in need. ※ Note: When deleting Bounding Volume, be aware that all corresponding Arrangement Points also get deleted from the 3D window. Select the Arrangement Points and assign them to another Bounding Volume to avoid any loss. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ Delete ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ Delete → Selected Bounding Volume is now being deleted from the Bounding Volume list and the 3D window. ※ Note: Selecting a Bounding Volume in the 3D window and pressing Delete key on keyboard also allows to delete it.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for safely deleting a Bounding Volume and its associated Arrangement Points in the Avatar Editor, ensuring users avoid unintentional data loss.

title: Trim (*.trm) Open/Save
content: ### Objective Save OBJ files as Trim files. Trim files can be previewed in the Marvelous Designer Library and can be glued to the Garment. ### Location #### Save Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Trim #### Open Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Trim ### Operation #### Save 1. Load an OBJ file as Trim. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below : Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Trim → When there are multiple OBJs in the 3D window, tje Save Trim window appears allowing you to choose the desired OBJ. → The Save File window appears. 3. Locate the saving path and file name. Then, click the Save button. → The OBJ file is saved Trim file. #### Open 1. Follow the indicated guideline below : Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Trim → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the file to be opened and click Open. → The Open Trim window appears. 3. Use the drop-down menu next to Position option to locate the Trim. → Original: trim is loaded at its original position when it was saved as a Trim file. → Reset: trim is loaded at the center of the 3D window. ※ Note: * Hover the mouse over the Trim file in the Library window to preview trim. * Click and drag or double lick the Trim file to open from the Library window.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for saving OBJ files as Trim files and accessing them in the Marvelous Designer Library for use in garment design.

title: ANIMATION MODE: Wind Animation
content: Save Wind animation property by frame (Ver. MD 7) ### Objective Create or delete wind animation key ### Location Animation Mode Animation Editor ### Operation **Creating Wind Animation Key** 1. Create a pattern to apply Wind animation. 2. Navigate to the menu indicated in Location. 3. Main menu>Display>Environment> Check 'Show Wind Controller' Can adjust wind property when Wind Controller is displayed. 4. Select the Wind controller and move Playhead to the frame where Wind animation key will be applied on Timeline Wind controller will move along intermediate value if move Playhead after Wind animation key is set, Need to move Playhead first before set wind property, in order to locate wind controller to desired position. 5. Wind property will displayed when select Wind controller on 3D window. Use Gizmo to adjust Wind controller's position and direction. Check properties want to apply and input value. Rotation and position of the wind are available to adjust by Gizmo on 3D window. 6. Right click on Playhead on time line. Select 'Add key' on popup menu to save wind property. Add key menu will not show up if wind controller is not selected. When Wind Animation key is set, Wind property values will be applied gradually to the next key. For example, if Wind strength of first frame is 500 and last frame is 1000, Wind strength will gradually increase 500 ~ 1000 from first frame to last frame. When Wind Animation key is set and there is no existing next Wind animation key, Wind property of the key will be applied from the key to the end of the frame. 7. Wind Property will be applied when recording animation. **Checking Wind Animation Key** 1. Check position and rotation of wind controller of each frame by moving Playhead on time line, after adding Wind Animation key on 3D window. **Deleting key** 1. Select Wind controller. 2. Wind Animation keys will be displayed on Animation timeline. 3. Select a key and right click. Select 'Delete Key' on pop up menu to delete selected Wind Animation key. 4. Available to delete multiple keys by Area select. Move Playhead to the start point of desired area and click the end of the area while pressing 'Shift' key. Delete all key of selected area by right click on selected area> select Delete Key on popup menu.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for creating, checking, and deleting wind animation keys in the Animation Editor, enabling users to effectively manage wind properties for their animations.

title: Deactivate(Pattern & Sewing)/Activate
content: ### Objective Deactivated Patterns are considered as nonexistence in the 3D window. Therefore the rest of the Patterns simulate through the deactivated Patterns. The function is generally used to keep complicated details such as pleats or slits, from avoiding collapsing (ver2.3.0). ※ Note: When deactivating certain Patterns, the Simulation speed gets faster as it excludes them from calculation. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) / Activate 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern ▶ 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) / Activate ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) / Activate 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern ▶ 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) / Activate → The selected Patterns and connected Sewing Lines are now being deactivated/activated. ※ Note: 3D Statement
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to deactivate and activate patterns in a 3D and 2D environment to optimize simulation speed and manage complex garment details.
